column3: Fertilizer shortage calendar phase 1: price shock, week 0-2
column9: DTN retail urea national avg $/ton: $573 (wk Jan 12-16) -> $677 (wk Mar 16-20) -> $838 peak (wk Mar 30-Apr 3), +34% MoM — largest monthly move of the cycle

column3: Fertilizer shortage calendar phase 2: inventory drawdown, week 2-4
column9: No free public instrument measures US fertilizer inventory at weekly cadence. Claim named no instrument, no unit, no threshold — ungradeable in either direction
column10: Never register a phase without a named instrument
column11: VOID not MISS: absence of a grading instrument is not evidence against the claim. Root cause of the class: finding_hypothesis_needs_an_instrument_for_its_defining_mechanism.

column3: Fertilizer shortage calendar phase 3: allocation crisis, week 4-6
column9: Real but NOT in the US: India IPL emergency tender 2.5 Mt in one tender (~1/4 of annual import need) awarded 1.5 Mt @ $935/mt CFR west + 1.0 Mt @ $959/mt CFR east, ~2x prior levels. NO US allocation or rationing event occurred
column10: Scope the geography in the claim text
column11: The March text implied US allocation. It fired offshore. Graded PARTIAL in the assessment; recorded here as HIT(partial) per Class-3 enum with the nuance parenthesised.

column3: Fertilizer shortage calendar phase 4: planting disruption, Apr-May
column9: REFUTED cleanly. US corn planting ran AHEAD of the 5-yr avg all season: 11% vs 9% (4/19), +4pp above 5-yr avg early May, 86% planted by 5/24 vs 79% soybeans. Emergence also above 5-yr avg. Farmers paid $838/ton retail and planted on time
column10: Affordability shock != physical allocation failure — do not infer one from the other
column11: The cleanest refutation in the record. Killed the physical-yield channel, which is the channel that carried the 1973 analog.

column3: Fertilizer shortage calendar phase 5: food CPI spike, Q3-Q4 2026
column9: First month of the predicted window: July food-at-home -0.07% m/m / +2.7% y/y (BLS CUSR0000SAF11 via FRED, 8/12 release). USDA ERS (7/24) forecasts FAH 2.7% 2026 / 2.9% 2027 driven by cattle herd at 75-yr low, avian flu, produce, wheat — fertilizer NOT cited. Input has round-tripped: Pink Sheet urea $856.9/mt Apr -> $400.0 Jul
column10: Do not re-open on a re-read of the same shock; requires a FRESH input shock
column11: Timing claim graded MISS; MECHANISM not refuted (finding_market_ignoring_is_not_market_refuting). Q4 formally open but the input that would drive it has reversed. Carried forward as an instrumented QUESTION, not a prediction.

column3: Registered threshold: urea NOLA >$800 = RED, triggers food CPI chain
column9: Post-mortem: (a) UNSATISFIABLE on its named benchmark — NOLA granular barge peaked ~$435/st in 2026 and has never traded near $800; (b) SIMULTANEOUSLY BREACHED ~8 weeks on the unnamed benchmark it was actually tracking (DTN retail $/ton, peak $838 Mar30-Apr3) and on India CFR ($935-959 Apr); (c) its stated implication did NOT follow when it breached — food-at-home -0.07% m/m in the first window month; (d) it fired in April into a dormant agent with no assigned grader and sat ~8 weeks ungraded; (e) it has since un-fired (NOLA $385-410/st 8/7/26)
column10: DO NOT RE-REGISTER in this form. Any replacement names benchmark+unit+source+revision policy
column11: Three independent failures in one line: benchmark mislabel, unit unstated, consequence unvalidated. Charter carries the do-not-re-register rule. Cross-ref finding_number_carries_threshold_unit_source + finding_fired_gate_needs_owner_independent_ledger.

column3: CF Industries: +$2.7B annualized EBITDA tailwind from +$167/ton urea
column9: CF 1H2026 (release 8/5/26): adj EBITDA $2.18B vs $1.41B = +$770M (+55%); net earnings $1.34B vs $698M (+92%). Realized annualized run-rate uplift ~$1.5B vs claimed $2.7B = ~1.8x OVERSTATED. And the uplift was earned in the half containing the entire price spike; H2 faces $678/ton retail and sub-$450 international
column10: Derive sensitivity from disclosed figures or do not state one
column11: Direction was the valuable call and it paid. The magnitude rested on an '$800M per $50/ton' sensitivity that is GENUINELY UNAVAILABLE — not disclosed by CF, not reproducible from filings. Charter forbids carrying it.

column3: Qatar 77 mtpa LNG offline = fertilizer capacity physically destroyed
column9: REFUTED on magnitude ~6x: actual 12.8 mtpa (Trains 4 & 6, Ras Laffan) = ~17% of Qatar export capacity, per QatarEnergy production update 3/20/26. 77 mtpa is Qatar's approximate TOTAL nameplate capacity — the denominator was recorded as the numerator. Repair timeline 3-5 yr CONFIRMED; cause (Iranian missile strikes 3/18-19/26) CONFIRMED. Separately: NO primary links the Ras Laffan LNG damage to ammonia/urea output
column10: Delete unevidenced mechanism inferences; state them as open questions
column11: The 6x error sat directly under the thesis's load-bearing word, 'structural'. Inference 'fertilizer production depends on same gas' remains UNVERIFIED and is deleted from the rebuilt STATUS rather than carried.

column3: China MOFCOM full export halt is permanent while Hormuz closed (scored 5/5, RED-RED)
column9: REFUTED as current. China reopened the urea export window end-May 2026 after ~8-month near-total suspension. 2026 quota 3.3 Mt total; ~2.0-2.5 Mt allocated Jun-Aug; CF projects 4-6 Mt actual exports. This is the PROXIMATE CAUSE of the ~50% global urea round-trip — Chinese offers into India below $400/t CFR by late July
column10: Never score a policy variable as a frozen constant; re-read at every wake
column11: THE vector that decided the outcome, and the only one the March desk froze. Charter now mandates re-reading the China row at every wake regardless of trigger state (T10 = guaranteed floor).

column3: India enters emergency/panic purchasing on Gulf supply loss (49% nitrogen from Gulf)
column9: CONFIRMED at scale on the predicted mechanism. IPL emergency tender Apr 2026: 2.5 Mt in a single tender, ~1/4 of annual import requirement, awarded $935/mt CFR west (1.5 Mt) / $959/mt CFR east (1.0 Mt), ~2x the rate of two months earlier
column11: The March desk's single best call and the highest-value one: it named the mechanism, the geography and the trigger, and all three landed. Retained as the model for how a FERT prediction should be written.
